conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Patel. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had this bad stomach pain for about four days now. It’s the same kind I’ve had before with my pancreas. But this time it’s going around to my back, left side.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I see you have a history of chronic pancreatitis. Any nausea or vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve thrown up a few times. And… there was a little blood in it, just streaks. Not a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, chills, or trouble urinating?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever. And I haven’t had any issues with my urine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright. Your vitals when you arrived showed a fast heart rate, but your labs came back normal. We gave you some fluids and medication for nausea and pain in the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, the Dilaudid helped a little. But the pain’s still there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to keep you on bowel rest for now—no food or drink by mouth—to let your pancreas calm down. You’ll get IV fluids and pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But what about the blood in my vomit? That scared me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely a small tear in the lining of your esophagus from vomiting. It’s called a Mallory-Weiss tear. It usually heals on its own, and your blood count is stable, so we’re not worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. That makes sense. I’ve thrown up a lot before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also did a chest X-ray to check your heart and lungs, since your heart rate was high. Everything looked clear—no pneumonia or fluid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. I’ve had a lot of medical stuff over the years.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I see you’ve had several ERCPs and even a Puestow procedure. We’ll continue your regular meds for diabetes, blood pressure, and mental health.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my metformin? Should I still take that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re holding it for now since you’re not eating. We’ll restart it when you’re back on a regular diet. You’ll keep taking your Lantus insulin at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my gabapentin and pancreas enzymes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart those once you start eating again. For now, we’re giving pain control with IV Dilaudid every few hours as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better, I think. The pain’s not as bad. And I haven’t thrown up since last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs this morning are stable. No signs of infection, and your kidney function is normal. The flank pain seems to be gone too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, that’s better. I was worried it was a kidney stone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your urine, and there’s no infection or blood. So it’s unlikely. We think the flank pain was just referred from your pancreas flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. Can I try drinking something now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start you on clear liquids—water, broth, apple juice. If you tolerate that, we’ll advance to solid food tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the diet going? Any nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had some broth and gelatin, and I’m okay. No throwing up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll switch your pain meds to oral—starting with something milder. No narcotics by mouth, but we’ll keep using the Dilaudid if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d rather not take strong painkillers if I don’t have to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re trying to avoid that. We’ll also restart your metformin and pancreatic enzymes with your next meal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well. You’ve been on a regular diet since last night, no vomiting, pain is manageable. We’d like to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good news. But what should I do to avoid another flare?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Stick to a low-fat diet, avoid alcohol completely, and take your pancreatic enzymes with every meal. Stay hydrated and keep managing your diabetes well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t had alcohol in years. But I know my diet’s been off lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could be the trigger. Even small dietary lapses can set it off. Continue all your regular medications as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Please schedule an appointment with your primary care doctor within the next week. Call us sooner if the pain comes back, or if you start vomiting again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I will. Thanks for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You’re alert, walking fine, and eating well—so you’re safe to go home. We’ll send your discharge papers shortly.
